text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced 2.8% today, recovering modestly after a brutal week that saw the stock drop 7% from late October highs. The rebound likely reflects relief that refining conditions remain strong—U.S. refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with tight fuel supplies, and the company just announced a leadership change and company update on October 29th, which may have cleared uncertainty. Oil prices remain elevated (U.S. crude at $103, global at $123), supporting margins for refiners that turn crude into gasoline and diesel.

The broader context is that political scrutiny of Big Oil profits has intensified this week—Trump criticized energy companies for excessive earnings—yet refining fundamentals actually support those margins right now. Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continues despite Iranian escalation, meaning crude supply disruptions haven't materialized, and storage levels (693M barrels of crude, 209M of gasoline, 103M of diesel) show fuel demand is absorbing supply without overwhelming the market. Today's gain is a small pullback in a volatile week rather than a reversal of the downtrend.
